name: Darius
overview: Darius was a male king of Persia mentioned in the book of Ezra. He is likely identified as Darius III, the last King of Persia who was conquered by Alexander the Great. His role as a Persian monarch situates him within the broader biblical narrative concerning the nations interacting with Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Darius means 'he who upholds the good,' reflecting a positive attribute though not given by God. He is also referred to by several titles including 'King of Persia,' 'King Darius,' 'King of Assyria,' and 'Darius the Persian,' indicating his royal status and association with Persian and Assyrian domains as recorded in Ezra and Nehemiah.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Darius beyond his identification as king. There are no listed relationships or tribal affiliations connected to him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Darius holds significance as a Persian king who appears in the biblical record during the post-exilic period, a time when the Persian Empire exerted influence over Israel. His reign provides historical context for the restoration efforts described in Ezra and Nehemiah. The mention of Darius underscores God's sovereign use of foreign rulers in His providential plan for His people.
